Summary and interpretation with Beige Book context:
- Policy: FOMC held the target range at 4.25–4.50% and will continue QT. Risks to the dual mandate are described as roughly balanced, with inflation “somewhat elevated,” and the Committee remaining data-dependent.
- SLOOS read-through: Loan demand appears firmer across C&I and key consumer categories, while standards remain tighter and banks expect higher delinquencies; CRE lending conditions stay cautious. This combination nudges the communication modestly hawkish versus a purely “balanced” stance.
- Beige Book context (Jan 6, 2025, prepared by the Chicago Fed): District reports point to modest, uneven expansion with ongoing CRE stress and tighter credit-sensitive conditions; contacts noted mixed consumer spending and some easing in wage/price pressures in parts of the country. These observations temper the SLOOS-driven hawkish tilt by underscoring pockets of softness and downside risks.

Net: Still slightly hawkish overall, but the Beige Book’s mixed/mild growth and CRE stress soften the tilt.
